topic: Fix p>=2 labeled coordinates and an unordered collection of p+1 distinct centered nonsingular Gaussian components generated by one observational acyclic linear Gaussian SEM plus exactly one effective perfect stochastic intervention per node. Do not assume faithfulness; require root interventions to change variance, allow nonroot marginal variance preservation, and condition stability on all component covariances rather than the baseline alone. Correct the ICML 2023 Proposition 10 rank selector with legal p=2 and p=3 counterfamilies. Prove universal recovery of the baseline, targets, DAG, and parameters via coordinate-isolated precision pairs, invariant root marginals, and unique row-support matching; prove a sound-and-complete O(p^4) real-arithmetic membership certificate checking baseline factorization and every surgery; and prove stability under operator error < min(lambda/2, alpha lambda^2/16, g/8), where lambda is the minimum eigenvalue across all components, alpha is the relevant precision support margin, and g is the root marginal gap. Include an open-family impossibility theorem for permutation-equivariant rank-only baseline selectors and evaluate the certificate as a semantic validation layer for causaldag's documented unknown-target IGSP mixture workflow. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Universal baseline orientation, unique target matching, full parameter recovery, membership soundness/completeness, and the resolvent threshold have complete proof spines; fresh exact checks passed 296 legal models, 296 relabelings, an independent small-dimensional explanation enumeration, 200 within-radius perturbations, and four exact near-singular instances. The corrected necessity witness has alpha=1/2. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Derive a concrete unordered Gaussian-component estimator with an explicit operator-error tail T_n(delta) for growing p; current statistical claims are conditional on component estimation. EARLY KILL TEST: Accept both p=2 witnesses and six p=3 legal examples under independent reconstruction; reject the p=3 false positive at baseline factorization; at t=1/100 verify alpha=1/2, positive-definite perturbed covariance, and precision off-diagonal magnitudes 103/97, 1, and 200/97. open_problems.open_problem: For an unordered collection of one observational and one centered perfect-stochastic-intervention Gaussian component per labeled node, determine a permutation-equivariant criterion that recovers the observational baseline, target bijection, DAG, and SEM parameters without faithfulness, replacing the deviation-rank selector of Squires et al. (2023).

source_refs.claim: Proposition 10 claims that the observational context is the unique minimizer of a sum of pairwise precision-difference ranks; the topic's legal low-dimensional families falsify that selector.
source_refs.author: Chandler Squires, Anna Seigal, Salil S. Bhate, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: Its mixture-to-causal-discovery corollary supplies the observational distribution separately and invokes UT-IGSP under interventional faithfulness, so it does not recover a hidden baseline from the unordered components.
source_refs.author: Abhinav Kumar, Kirankumar Shiragur, Caroline Uhler

open_problems.why_unsolved: The only located population reduction from an unknown observational context is the Proposition 10 rank rule, while the later mixture paper bypasses baseline selection by supplying observational samples separately. Rank is permutation invariant but too coarse: root and nonroot perfect interventions can generate tied or reversed pairwise-rank patterns, and a low-rank collection can fail to be any common-baseline surgery model. A replacement must use the support and factorization geometry of precision pairs, prove unique row matching, and reject algebraic impostors; neither cited paper provides that characterization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit recovery map from the unordered covariance set to the baseline index, node-target permutation, DAG, edge coefficients, and noise variances, plus legal low-dimensional counterfamilies to the rank rule and a sound-and-complete algebraic membership certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation proceeds from unknown intervention contexts to full latent structural recovery and isolates observational-context selection as the missing preprocessing step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: interventional contexts can identify a linear Gaussian causal representation -> context and target labels may be unknown -> pairwise precision changes encode intervention geometry -> a correct baseline-and-target recovery criterion is required

method_exemplars.technique: Retain its precision-difference and partial-order RQ reconstruction after a baseline is fixed, but replace the rank-sum baseline step by support-sensitive perfect-surgery identities and factorization checks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It reconstructs the same Gaussian SEM objects from one intervention per node and exposes exactly where unknown context labels enter.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its Lasso-type quadratic estimator of sparse precision differences and its entrywise-concentration/minimum-change support-recovery proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The corrected population map is driven by supports of precision differences, so this is the nearest finite-sample support-estimation machinery.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a concrete estimator of the p+1 unordered centered Gaussian components from pooled mixture samples, for p growing, with an explicit high-probability operator-norm error tail strong enough to trigger the deterministic causal-recovery margin.

source_refs.claim: Its proved Gaussian-mixture parameter learner assumes a fixed number of components, leaving the p+1 growing-component regime outside the causal corollary's guarantee.
source_refs.author: Abhinav Kumar, Kirankumar Shiragur, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: It clusters TV-separated mixtures of centered Gaussians with arbitrary covariances using dependence on the minimum mixing weight rather than d^{O(k)}, but does not provide the intervention-specific operator-error interface.
source_refs.author: Prashanti Anderson, Mitali Bafna, Rares-Darius Buhai, Pravesh K. Kothari, David Steurer

source_refs.claim: General Gaussian-mixture parameter learning has dependence exponential in the component count, with such dependence necessary absent additional structure.
source_refs.author: Ankur Moitra, Gregory Valiant

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the Chebyshev radius with a covariance-specific concentration construction
no statistical rate is claimed without explicit covariance-region inputs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature reaches the pooled intervention problem only for fixed component count or reaches growing centered mixtures under generic TV separation, whereas the prior CausalSmith programs start from labeled covariance statistics or externally supplied covariance regions. Here k=p+1 and the regime label is latent: one must first derive quantitative component separation from the perfect-surgery parameters, control label switching and clustering errors, and only then apply covariance concentration and inverse perturbation. General-mixture results can be exponential in p, while the newer growing-k result does not translate surgery margins into its TV assumption or state the post-clustering operator-norm tail consumed by the alpha/lambda/g recovery threshold.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An implementable estimator and an explicit T_n(delta; p, pi_min, spectral envelope, separation) with probability at least 1-delta that the maximum permutation-matched covariance operator error is at most T_n(delta), plus a sample-size corollary making T_n(delta) < min(lambda/2, alpha lambda^2/16, g/8).

writing_exemplar.why: It frames pooled interventional data as a Gaussian-mixture problem and marks fixed component count as the unresolved boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: intervention noise pools observational and interventional units -> the pooled law is a Gaussian mixture -> causal discovery first requires component recovery -> p+1 growing components require a nonperturbative operator-error guarantee

method_exemplars.technique: Apply its sum-of-squares separation-preserving projection and recursive partial-clustering proof for centered nonspherical mixtures, then estimate each recovered cluster covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination mixture is centered with arbitrary unequal covariances and k grows with dimension, matching the paper's target regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Use effective-rank Gaussian sample-covariance concentration to obtain the required operator-norm tail within each approximately recovered cluster.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once assignments are controlled, it gives the exact norm and tail form needed for covariance inversion and deterministic support stability.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its projection, hierarchical clustering, rescaling, and permutation matching that convert univariate mixture recovery into multivariate parameter recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly outputs component parameters up to permutation and reveals which component-count dependence the SEM restrictions must remove.

open_problems.open_problem: Turn the exact perfect-intervention Gaussian membership certificate into a finite-sample test or abstaining validator with uniform type-I control and power against unordered component collections separated from the model.

source_refs.claim: Its appendix states that rank at most two is only necessary, leaves a full membership test to future work, and separately leaves an inverse-Wishart-minor test with false-discovery guarantees open.
source_refs.author: Chandler Squires, Anna Seigal, Salil S. Bhate, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: It derives first and second moments of fixed-size minors of Wishart sample covariance matrices for testing polynomial covariance constraints.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Helene Massam, Ingram Olkin

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ICML statistic screens a necessary rank condition that admits population false positives; it does not test common-baseline factorization or every perfect surgery. A complete semantic certificate couples equalities, support decisions, positive-definiteness inequalities, and a discrete target matching, while mixture-estimated covariances are dependent and label switched. Wishart-minor formulas apply to segregated sample covariances rather than inverse covariances obtained after latent mixture assignment, so they do not supply uniform calibration or simultaneous error control for the full certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable accept/reject/abstain rule with model-uniform rejection probability at most eta and power at least 1-beta against every unordered component collection epsilon-separated from the certified model, with explicit dependence on n, p, pi_min, and epsilon.

writing_exemplar.why: Its appendix motivates model checking, distinguishes necessary rank restrictions from full membership, and identifies the missing calibration problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: identification assumes every component is a legal single-node intervention -> empirical mixtures may violate that semantic model -> low-rank screening is necessary but not sufficient -> a sound and powerful full-membership validator is needed

method_exemplars.technique: Use sample minors and compound-Wishart moment identities to studentize and jointly test the polynomial rank and factorization constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rank and factorization portions of the desired certificate are polynomial minor constraints, exactly the class treated by this paper.

method_exemplars.technique: Build simultaneous operator-norm confidence balls for the component covariances and propagate them through inverse perturbation bounds and certificate inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A confidence-ball wrapper naturally supports honest abstention near the membership boundary.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly which baseline-DAG edges and SEM parameters are identifiable from an unordered observational-plus-perfect-intervention Gaussian collection when fewer than p distinct nodes are intervened on.

source_refs.claim: Its discussion calls for a theory of latent interventional Markov equivalence for K
source_refs.author: Chandler Squires, Anna Seigal, Salil S. Bhate, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: It characterizes an equivalence class of Gaussian SCMs across segregated environments with unknown noise-intervention targets under faithfulness and intervention heterogeneity.
source_refs.author: Juan L. Gamella, Armeen Taeb, Christina Heinze-Deml, Peter Buhlmann

open_problems.why_unsolved: Worst-case failure of full recovery does not identify which structural rows, ancestor relations, edge orientations, or parameter combinations remain determined by a particular collection. Existing interventional-equivalence results assume segregated environments and faithfulness or target-set information; they do not include an unknown baseline inside an unordered list of perfect surgeries. The complete-coverage proof's unique row-support matching fails first: unmatched coordinates have no surgery witness, so recovery must become a sharp set-valued equivalence relation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient observational equivalence relation for unordered K+1 covariance collections, an algorithm returning the sharp identified set of DAGs and SEM rows, and indistinguishable model pairs proving completeness for every unresolved edge or parameter.

writing_exemplar.why: It poses the K
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: one intervention per node can give full recovery -> realistic experiments omit nodes -> worst-case impossibility need not erase all information -> the partially identified causal object must be characterized

method_exemplars.technique: Define distributional equivalence through common structural coefficients and environment-specific noise variances, then prove a graphical characterization of the equivalence class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest set-valued identification proof for Gaussian unknown-target interventions.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate precision-difference supports on recursively chosen variable subsets and use minimum-signal arguments to recover visible targets and parents.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Recursively visible supports are natural estimable summaries of the rows and orientations that remain identified under incomplete intervention coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Replace exact one-node perfect surgeries by quantitatively approximate surgeries and characterize the largest observable off-target residual under which a compatibility family contains the true baseline, target matching, and DAG and collapses to a singleton under separation.

source_refs.excerpt: Develop an approximate common-range/reference extension with an observable residual tolerance

open_problems.why_unsolved: Operator perturbation of an exact member and structural misspecification are different: a small off-target mechanism change can systematically violate coordinate-isolated precision-pair zeros even with infinite data. The first exact-proof step that fails is support isolation; it must be replaced by a residual-tolerant compatibility relation whose false inclusions are controlled by a structural separation margin, rather than treating misspecification as covariance sampling error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound outer compatibility map indexed by an observable off-target residual, a sufficient-condition theorem for singleton collapse to the baseline/targets/DAG, and a positive-definite counterfamily proving failure or nonidentifiability beyond the stated threshold.

writing_exemplar.why: Its candidate-set framing for unknown intervention targets is the right narrative for a misspecification-robust outer family.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: intervention targets are unknown -> observable restrictions yield candidate target sets -> imperfect interventions violate exact restrictions -> residual-tolerant outer families should retain truth and collapse under separation

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt joint-diagonalization sensitivity expansions and their separation denominators to control perturbations of coordinate-isolation identities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems turn an exact algebraic diagonal/support identity into a quantitative uniqueness statement governed by a separation margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert tests over structural alternatives so the residual-tolerant target/DAG family has finite-sample coverage before singleton reporting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution is set valued near the boundary and therefore needs coverage-preserving abstention rather than an unconditional plug-in selector.
